parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/application/OrderService.ts is an application service. Its methods (placeOrder, advanceOrder, cancelOrder, listOrders) coordinate use cases: they load aggregates through repository interfaces defined in the domain layer, call domain behaviour (Order.advanceTo, Order.cancel, product.reserve/release), save the results and map them to DTOs. These are all application-layer jobs. The file has no persistence code (no SQL, ORM or storage), no transport code (no HTTP, request or response handling) and no framework code. Business rules stay in the domain: status changes and cancellation rules live in Order, and stock rules live in Product. Two parts are borderline. combineItems validates and merges input items, which counts as normalising and validating use-case input. The compensating release of reservations in placeOrder is cross-aggregate coordination. Both are reasonable in the application layer, and newId (ID generation) and toDto (DTO mapping) are too. One small point: the positive-integer quantity check could arguably be a domain invariant. But it works here as input validation, and there is no ADR text saying otherwise, so it is not a clear misplacement.
